canonical_title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber
treatment: Covered as a model release. Reinclude only for GA/pricing changes, material model-card or benchmark corrections, Fairwind access-policy changes, major independent evaluations, or production adoption/breakage.
known_facts: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash three weeks after 3.7 Flash, describing it as its most intelligent Flash workhorse for software engineering, agentic tasks and multi-step reasoning.
Gemini 3.8 Flash keeps the introductory developer price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, based on the same foundational intelligence but specialized for vulnerability detection and automated patching.
Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is limited to trusted defenders through Google's new Fairwind Program.
Google says both variants use long-running agentic loops that recursively evaluate and refine task execution.
Google reports 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 86.2% on CyberGym for Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber; these are vendor-reported results pending broader independent replication.
reinclude_only_if: Google changes pricing, availability, context/output limits, or production model identifiers.
Google publishes a material system/model card update or corrects reported benchmark results.
Independent reproducible evaluations materially change the interpretation of coding, agentic, cyber, cost, or token-efficiency performance.
Fairwind materially changes access criteria or Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber becomes broadly available.
A major production adoption, outage, regression, or safety incident changes practical interpretation.
notes: NEW for the 2026-09-03 Midday window. Google announced the models on Sep 2 US time; multiple timestamped reports place the launch well after the prior 2026-09-02 23:30 JST Night boundary.
